notes: Authored peer sets for the PRIVATE peer-set study lane
(scripts/peer_set_profiles.py, dispatched by
.github/workflows/corpus-peerset.yml). Output is counts only — roles,
techniques, evidence-record classes, legal postures — written to the
private bucket export prefix. It is NEVER a public RESEARCH surface.
A firm MATCH means the firm's name appears in the stored record
(title + clean_text + summary + ai_summary; enrichment_history is never
scanned). Presence in the record, never fault: the firm may be the
victim, the plaintiff, the defendant's former employer, or a bystander
named in passing. The report's reading rules say so verbatim.
MATCHING SEMANTICS mirror shared/data/vendor_aliases.json: case-
insensitive, word-boundary (an alias matches only when not butted
against another letter/digit on either side), multi-word aliases
tolerate any whitespace run, longest alias first.
Fidelity: NEVER bare 'Fidelity' — a common English word ('fidelity to
the contract') and a bond-insurance term (fidelity bond, fidelity
coverage) that appears in exactly the embezzlement cases this corpus
collects. Only the qualified names count.
Voya: COURTLISTENER_COMPANY_WATCHLIST defaults to 'Voya, Voya India'
(shared/settings.py), so Voya-named US filings are collected BY
CONSTRUCTION. The Voya count is a collection artifact, not a base rate;
the report carries the caveat in its appendix.
rules: 1. An alias must be specific enough that a match in a court filing
almost certainly names the firm. Single common English words are
FORBIDDEN as bare aliases: 'Fidelity', 'Principal' ('principal
amount', 'principal place of business'), 'Lincoln' (the city, the
president, the car), 'Nationwide' (the adverb), 'Equitable' (equitable
relief, equitable tolling), 'Empower', 'Vanguard' (the noun). Those
firms use compound aliases only ('Fidelity Investments', 'Principal
Financial', 'Lincoln Financial', 'Nationwide Mutual', 'Equitable
Holdings', 'Empower Retirement', 'Vanguard Group').
2. Single-token aliases are allowed ONLY from single_token_ok below:
coined names with no common-English collision (Voya, TIAA, MetLife,
Manulife, Transamerica, Aegon, PGIM). Every other alias must be at
least two whitespace-separated tokens.
3. Word-boundary matching is load-bearing: 'Voyager' must never credit
Voya, 'principal amount' must never credit Principal.
tests/test_peer_set_profiles.py pins both.
4. Former names count (ING U.S. -> Voya; Great-West Life -> Empower; AXA
Equitable -> Equitable; Teachers Insurance and Annuity -> TIAA) —
old court records name firms by the name of their era.
5. A parent named on its own (Manulife, Aegon) credits the peer firm it
owns (John Hancock, Transamerica): the study is about the group.
